title: Greywater Bay Rising Revisited
premise: When Greywater Bay's founder, Edmund Voss, is exhumed for a heritage ceremony, his coffin proves empty, and concierge Noor Halloran realizes the guest register she has kept for fifteen years holds the key to a thirty-year-old disappearance. As she cross-references old alibis with the town's founding families, she discovers that several of her closest friends — the surrogate family she built after losing her own — conspired to hide a death and protect one of their children. The empty coffin held not a body but a ledger of debts, and Noor must choose between exposing the truth that will shatter her found family or letting an innocent man, jailed decades ago for Voss's murder, die in prison. In the end she finds a third path: she forces the conspirators to confess publicly by threatening to reveal what she knows, freeing the wrongly convicted man while the town, furious but weary, chooses to absorb its own reckoning rather than destroy itself.
about_author: Astrid Galloway spent a decade working front desks in coastal hotels before turning to crime fiction, a career she credits for teaching her that every town keeps two ledgers. She lives in a fog-bound harbor town where she still greets strangers by name.

chapters.title: The Guest Who Never Left
chapters.summary: Noor Halloran, POV. During preparations for Greywater Bay's sesquicentennial, officials exhume founder Edmund Voss for a ceremonial reinterment and find the coffin empty except for a waterlogged ledger. Noor watches from the hotel lobby, recognizing the ledger's binding as identical to one she once shelved in the hotel safe. Beat: quiet dread beneath professional composure.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Check-Ins
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. Flashbacks interleave with the present as Noor reviews her meticulous guest registers, realizing the ledger matches entries from the year before her hiring. Her mentor, former concierge Ruthie, went silent about that era before dying. Noor pockets a page she shouldn't have. Beat: curiosity curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: The Empty Grave Society
chapters.summary: Detective Ivo Marsh, POV. Marsh, new to town, catches the case and immediately distrusts the founding families' smooth cooperation. He interviews Noor professionally; she gives him nothing but notices he asks about 1994 specifically. Beat: two careful professionals circling each other.

chapters.title: Alibis Woven in Wool
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. At the knitting circle she hosts — her found family: Marta, Delphine, and old Tomás — Noor casually raises the exhumation. Each friend offers an alibi for 1994 unprompted, too polished, too alike. Noor recognizes the weave because she was taught to spot fabricated stories at the front desk. Beat: betrayal's first cold touch.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Alphabet
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. Deciphering the waterlogged ledger, Noor finds names, dates, and sums — payments to silence someone named only 'W.' Cross-referencing hotel archives, she identifies Wren Okafor, a handyman convicted of Voss's murder in 1995, still imprisoned. Beat: the mystery gains a human stake.

chapters.title: Letters from Cell Block D
chapters.summary: Wren Okafor, POV (letters). Through letters to his late sister, Wren recounts his trial: three witnesses, all connected to the hotel, all certain. He has stopped proclaiming innocence years ago; hope is a luxury. His calm devastates Noor when she visits under a false name. Beat: guilt arrives wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: What Ruthie Knew
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. Searching Ruthie's sealed belongings, Noor finds a half-burned letter warning 'the third grave is not empty either.' She confronts Marta gently; Marta deflects with a story about a storm night and a knocked-over candle. Noor lets it go — and hates herself for it. Beat: loyalty begins bending toward lies.

chapters.title: The Founder's Daughter
chapters.summary: Cassian Voss, POV. Edmund's grandson Cassian, now a judge, pressures police to close the exhumation inquiry as vandalism. Privately he meets with Delphine and Tomás; we glimpse the machinery of protection without full revelation. He burns a document in his fireplace. Beat: power arranging the past.

chapters.title: Room 214 Keeps Its Secrets
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. A guest checks into Room 214 — the room where, per the ledger, 'W.' last worked the night Voss vanished. The guest is Wren's niece, investigating quietly. Noor must decide whether to help her or protect the hotel's owners, who employ half her friends. Beat: divided heart.

chapters.title: Storm Season Almanac
chapters.summary: Tomás, POV. Tomás recalls the October 1994 storm that cut the town off for nine days — no ferries, no phones. He remembers carrying something heavy wrapped in tarpaulin to the boathouse, telling himself it was salvage. His chapter ends mid-memory, refusing to finish. Beat: memory as self-defense.

chapters.title: The Third Grave
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. Following Ruthie's clue, Noor locates a third unmarked grave behind the decommissioned lighthouse. It contains not a body but a strongbox: Voss's real accounting, proving he was blackmailing four townspeople over a fire that killed a migrant worker — Wren's brother. Beat: the moral ground shifts entirely.

chapters.title: Everyone Paid Something
chapters.summary: Delphine, POV. Delphine narrates 1994 plainly at last: Voss died of a heart attack during a confrontation, and the four panicked, hiding the body and framing Wren, who had motive and no alibi. They weren't murderers, she insists — they were frightened people who became liars. Beat: sympathy weaponized against justice.

chapters.title: Confession at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. Noor confronts the four together in the boathouse where it began. They offer her membership in the secret — a place in the family, forever — if she stays silent. She walks out into the tide flats, shaking, understanding exactly what she'd be buying. Beat: the offer that costs everything.

chapters.title: Marsh Suspects Everyone
chapters.summary: Ivo Marsh, POV. Marsh narrows in on the 1994 witness statements, finding they share phrasing no independent witnesses would use. He subpoenas the hotel archives; Noor must decide whether to hand over the stolen ledger page or destroy it. She copies it first. Beat: the law closing in on both guilty and innocent.

chapters.title: The Knitting Circle Unravels
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. Marta, the conscience of the group, breaks: she has been leaving anonymous money for Wren's family for twenty years. She begs Noor to find another way than public ruin. Their friendship fractures along the fault line between mercy and truth. Beat: love and honesty declared incompatible.

chapters.title: Deadline: The Sesquicentennial
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. Cassian announces the reburial ceremony with a new, sealed coffin — entombing the question forever. Noor realizes the town's ritual amnesia will become permanent unless she acts within ten days. She drafts a letter to the parole board about Wren and hesitates over the send button. Beat: ticking clock made personal.

chapters.title: What the Register Remembers
chapters.summary: Ivo Marsh, POV. Marsh finally reads the hotel registers and finds the same anomaly Noor did: four rooms booked under false names the week Voss vanished, all paid from one account — Cassian's. He comes to Noor not to arrest her but to ask what she's been carrying. Beat: alliance forming across professional lines.

chapters.title: The Longest Night Shift
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. Someone ransacks the archive room; the original ledger page is gone, but Noor's copy survives hidden in plain sight in a guest folio. She suspects Tomás, who leaves a note: 'They know you know. Protect yourself, not us.' Fear becomes concrete. Beat: threat inside the family.

chapters.title: Reburial
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. At the ceremony, as the new coffin lowers, Noor steps forward with the microphone meant for Cassian's address and reads the ledger aloud — names, sums, the fire, the brother, the frame. The town goes silent as the coffin settles into a grave holding no truth at all. Beat: climax; the secret dies publicly so the truth can live.

chapters.title: Arrests and Accomplices
chapters.summary: Ivo Marsh, POV. Marsh arrests the three surviving conspirators; Cassian resigns rather than face impeachment. Wren's conviction is vacated on newly surfaced evidence Noor and Marsh assembled together. Marsh tells Noor she obstructed as much as she revealed — and chooses not to pursue it. Beat: justice, imperfect and purchased.

chapters.title: Checking Out
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. Wren walks free into a town that owes him everything and apologizes for nothing; Noor drives him past the lighthouse and gives him his brother's strongbox. Marta comes to the desk to check out — leaving town, not the friendship. Some accounts stay open. Beat: grief and forgiveness sharing a room.

chapters.title: Greywater Bay Rising
chapters.summary: Noor, POV, one year later. The hotel has a new owner; the register continues. Noor trains a young concierge, teaching her to notice everything and choose carefully what to keep. On the anniversary, the whole town attends a small, honest memorial for the Okafor brothers. Noor files the past at last — alphabetized, but no longer hidden. Beat: resolution; a keeper of secrets becomes a keeper of record.
